Treatment plant locations: figures for review

Verified corrections, location sources, and the multi-source pipeline

Published

November 9, 2026

Data: master layer CWNS_Locations_20261014 (17,874 treatment plants, 3,068 verified), and the multi-source pipeline output (17,874 plants). A verified correction is a treatment plant with Verified = "Yes", Original_Correct = "No" and a corrected point; its distance is the great-circle distance from the reported CWNS point to the corrected point.

Headline numbers

Slide 11 Now
Verified corrections 316 841
Median correction distance 0.80 mi 0.35 mi
Mean correction distance 3.14 mi 1.52 mi
Corrections of 10 mi or more 20 21
Verified plants whose reported location was wrong ~40% 27% (841 of 3,068)

Also: 40% of corrections moved half a mile or more, 22% a mile or more, 5% five miles or more; the largest is 207 mi. The mean without the corrections of 10 mi or more is 0.80 mi.

Why the numbers fell. 451 of the corrections are model proposals a reviewer confirmed. The model searches near the reported point, so these are short: median 0.20 mi, longest 3.9 mi. The 295 reviewer-placed corrections still look like slide 11: median 0.81 mi, mean 3.26 mi. Reviewed plants were prioritised, not sampled at random, so neither the old ~40% nor the new 27% is a national error rate.

Where the right location comes from

Sources, as the pipeline names them: CWNS coordinate (cwns_point, the reported location), CWNS address geocode (cwns_addr), ICIS facility coordinate from FRS for a linked NPDES permit (icis_fac_frs), ICIS address geocode of that permit (icis_fac_addr), and ICIS permit features inside the plant: influent structure (icis_feat_INF) and internal outfall (icis_feat_INO). CWNS and ICIS are separate systems, but the two address geocodes often land on the same point, so they are shown together where they tie.

The CWNS coordinate is wrong for every plant here by definition (these are the corrected ones). Where it is within 250 m, a reviewer still judged it to be in the wrong place.

Fig 6. The source closest to the verified location

Rolled up: an ICIS source alone was closest for 52%, the CWNS coordinate for 18%, the CWNS address geocode alone for 8%, and the two address geocodes tied for 19%.

Stage 1 accepts a site that another source points to, so its new locations come mostly from ICIS. Stage 2 picks a candidate parcel near the reported point, so the CWNS coordinate is often the nearest source: the new parcel is usually a neighbour of the reported one.

Medians: Stage 2 moves 0.20 mi, Stage 1 site accepts 0.24 mi, verified corrections 0.35 mi. 105 pipeline moves exceed 5 km; they were kept as moves (decision of 6 Nov 2026).

Fig 10. Frozen holdout: single-seed against multi-source

Fig 11. The same plants, paired

Misplaced plants: outcome in each run (rows single-seed, columns multi-source)
accepted_right accepted_wrong flagged_wrong moved_right not_scored
accepted_reported 2 1 1 1 0
flagged_wrong 2 1 10 9 0
moved_right 13 1 0 7 0
not_scored 0 0 0 0 2

Paired result. On the 50 misplaced plants, multi-source put 14 right that single-seed got wrong and lost 1 (exact McNemar p = 0.001), so the gain is real, not noise. Most of it comes from Stage 2, not Stage 1: 10 plants were moved to the right parcel by multi-source’s Stage 2 where single-seed got them wrong, against 4 that multi-source’s Stage 1 accepted outright. Of the 17 plants multi-source’s Stage 1 got right, 13 were already right in single-seed through Stage 2; Stage 1 now reaches them earlier. On the 281 correct plants the runs differ on 10 (4 better, 6 worse, p = 0.75): no detectable change in false moves.

Caveats

  • Verified plants were chosen for review, not sampled at random: shares of plants found wrong are not national rates.
  • Model-proposed corrections are short by construction, which pulls the median and mean down.
  • The CWNS and ICIS address geocodes often coincide; count them as one piece of evidence.
  • Distances are point to point. A large plant can be correctly located 250 m or more from a source point.
  • The master here is the copy of 26 Oct 2026 (CWNS_Locations_20261014); reviews after that are not included.
